clue.text: Beef too? Why not!

parts.note: beef is muscle or strength, which is might
too means in addition, as well

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to have beef as well, and answers themselves cheerfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like the meat, but here it is muscle power.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom of shrugging agreement: there is no reason not to.

clue.text: The little darlings turned up to walk the dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to step is to walk
a pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog

explanation.surface: Children excitedly arrive to take the dog out for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses STEP and POM together, giving the letters in the opposite order.
explanation.definitionFit: Moppets are small, endearing children, little darlings.

clue.text: On the subject of gun belts, is excellent

indicators.note: belts means goes round the waist of, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun
re means concerning, on the subject of

explanation.surface: A remark praising someone's gun belts as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belts' looks like a noun about holsters, but it is a verb: the gun goes round the other piece. Gat is American gangster slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Great is everyday praise meaning very good or superb.

clue.text: Resembled, in being grasping?

definitions.meaning: to look like a parent is to resemble them
read literally, someone who took something after another was grabbing at it

explanation.definitionFit: Taking after a relative means resembling them, and literally a grasper takes after things.

clue.text: Don't keep on! It's only intended for storage

definitions.meaning: to cast off, as a snake its skin or a person clothing
a garden hut for keeping tools

explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off rather than keep wearing; a shed is a hut for keeping things.

clue.text: Happily dealt with trouble in the cathedral city

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters are placed within the city name

parts.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of dealt are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully handled a disturbance in a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the letters of 'dealt' to make LATED. Ely is a small city near Cambridge, famous for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Elatedly means in a joyful, exhilarated way.

clue.text: Get off — it's not serious

definitions.meaning: an old verb for dismount or alight
... reading or ... entertainment is not weighty

explanation.definitionFit: Light can mean to alight from a horse, and also trivial or unweighty.

clue.text: Quite happy to deceive over accommodation

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to con is to deceive
a tent is camping accommodation

explanation.surface: Someone is perfectly willing to lie about where they are staying.
explanation.definitionFit: Content means satisfied, pleased enough.

clue.text: Don't notice what you have under your very eyes?

definitions.meaning: to miss or fail to see something

definitions.text: what you have under your very eyes
definitions.meaning: a view from above looking down on what lies below

explanation.definitionFit: To overlook is to miss something; an overlook is a high vantage point giving a view below.

clue.text: Strange things seen by only women in the scrap heap?

definitions.text: Strange things seen by only women in the scrap heap?

parts.words: Strange things seen by only women in the scrap heap
parts.note: remarkable occurrences, with a playful split of the word into a hen and an 'o men' sitting inside a heap

explanation.surface: Odd sights spotted by a group of women rummaging in a junkyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke splits the word as P-HEN-O-MEN-A: a hen, with no men, in a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable or unusual occurrences are called by this plural.

clue.text: Prone to, granted

definitions.meaning: inclined towards
accepted or assumed

explanation.definitionFit: Given to means inclined towards; given means taken as granted.

clue.text: Runs that prove costly if not bargained for?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, runs not scored off the bat such as byes and wides

definitions.text: that prove costly if not bargained for
definitions.meaning: additional charges added to a bill

explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's byes, wides and no-balls count as extras; extras are also add-on charges beyond a quoted price.

clue.text: Travelled as a stowaway and wasn't punished

definitions.meaning: journeyed without paying a fare
was released without penalty

explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway's journey costs nothing; a released suspect escapes penalty.

clue.text: Unruffled, points to the day on the calendar

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
a date is a day on the calendar

explanation.surface: A calm person indicates today's date on the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and composed.

clue.text: Instrument, not quite blunt, with which the crime was perpetrated

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word for blunt is dropped

parts.note: dull means blunt, not sharp

indicators.note: perpetrated suggests something done or worked, so the letters of crime are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective's account of a blunt instrument used in a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was perpetrated' rearranges the letters of 'crime' to make CIMER. The surface makes 'Instrument' sound like a murder weapon, but it is a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A dulcimer is a stringed instrument played with hammers.

clue.text: During the fight don't have a loss of consciousness

indicators.note: during means the second piece sits inside the time of the fight

parts.note: a bout is a fight in boxing or wrestling
to lack is not to have

explanation.surface: Advice to a boxer not to faint mid-fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a temporary fainting, a loss of awareness.

clue.text: The broken heart I can mend, lady

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the following words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone vows to repair a broken heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges HEART, I and CAN; 'mend' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherina is a woman's name, as in Shakespeare's shrew.

clue.text: How the notabilities get on together?

definitions.text: How the notabilities get on together?

parts.words: How the notabilities get on together
parts.note: people get on extremely well, and famous people would do so in a way matching their fame

explanation.surface: A question about how celebrities relate to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on this way is an idiom for getting on very well, punned on celebrity.

clue.text: As the bulletin is by the erudite newscaster?

definitions.text: As the bulletin is by the erudite newscaster?

parts.words: As the bulletin is by the erudite newscaster
parts.note: a learned announcer is cultured, and the news he delivers is delivered skilfully

explanation.surface: A remark on how a learned newsreader delivers the bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learned through books is erudite, and a bulletin delivered skilfully is spoken nicely too.

clue.text: Strike, furious, with the whip

parts.note: wild means furious, enraged
the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out in fury with a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: A wildcat strike is a sudden unofficial walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial industrial walkout is called this, as a noun.

clue.text: Posts for the horse race

definitions.meaning: pointed wooden posts driven into the ground
a race in which owners put up prize money

explanation.definitionFit: Stakes are wooden posts, and many horse races carry the name, from the money put up.

clue.text: And entering isn't bent double

indicators.note: entering means the first word goes inside the rearranged letters
bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement about entering without stooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' makes STIN from ISNT; AND enters it. 'double' is a noun: a substitute actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in replaces a film actor, a body double.

clue.text: Hiding in a tunnel too small to stand up in?

definitions.meaning: keeping out of sight

definitions.text: in a tunnel too small to stand up in
definitions.meaning: literally stretched flat close to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Lying low is an idiom for keeping hidden; literally it is being flat on the ground.

clue.text: Without a single gram, we can't help him

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the gram abbreviation surrounds the other piece

parts.note: gr is an abbreviation for gram
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A lament that, lacking even a gram of something, a person cannot be saved.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone past saving, beyond help.

clue.text: One's rattled by the artist, a foreign lady

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: one's read as one is, giving the letters of the word with S
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled by a painter and a woman from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Senora is the Spanish title for a married woman, a lady.

clue.text: Belonging to someone, one conceded

definitions.meaning: possessed by a person
admitted, as in ... up

explanation.definitionFit: Something possessed is held by its owner; to own a fault is to admit it.

clue.text: Shout "Well said!"

indicators.note: said means the word for well is spoken, and its sound is entered

parts.note: hale means well, healthy

explanation.surface: A cry of approval at a fine speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail is to call out to someone.

clue.text: Family English to the core-completely

indicators.note: to the core means put into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

explanation.surface: A family that is English through and through.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean as an adverb means entirely, as in clean forgot.

clue.text: Posted off to Diane on the way

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the first piece is followed by the second

parts.note: ST is street, a way

indicators.note: off means going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter mailed to Diane along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to a base is stationed there.

clue.text: It means a ruler was used to open a cell door

definitions.text: It means a ruler was used to open a cell door

parts.words: It means a ruler was used to open a cell door
parts.note: a monarch's act of mercy frees a prisoner, not a measuring stick

explanation.surface: Someone forced a prison cell open with a measuring stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign's pardon frees a convict, so a ruler gets a cell opened.
